tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive solve after placing largest
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After moving the current largest disk that is not yet in its final position onto its goal peg, treat the remaining disks as a smaller sub‑problem and solve it recursively.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the largest misplaced disk can be moved legally to its goal peg and larger disks are already correctly placed below it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a larger disk onto a peg that still contains smaller disks, causing a dead‑end later.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Standard recursive transfer of k disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of k disks from a source peg to a target peg using an auxiliary peg, first recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the kth disk to the target, and finally move the k‑1 disks from the auxiliary onto the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to relocate a clean stack of consecutive disks from one peg to another.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a stack without first clearing the smaller disks, resulting in an illegal placement.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable block
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The answer must consist of a single syntactically correct Python‑style list of moves; the verifier reads the last parseable list in the response.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When formatting the final answer for the evaluator.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Appending explanatory text after the list, causing the parser to stop before the full move sequence.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration before output
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Mentally replay each move from the initial state and confirm that the resulting arrangement matches the goal before submitting the move list.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After generating the move list, before producing the final answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves a disk on the wrong peg because the final state was not double‑checked.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Provide only the move list, no extra text
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The response should contain only the move list; any additional text can be interpreted as part of the list and cause parsing errors.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When writing the final answer to be parsed by the verifier.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including a sentence like "Here is the solution:" before the list, leading to an empty or malformed parsed list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate legality of each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, ensure the source peg's top disk matches the moving disk and that the destination peg's top disk (if any) is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During construction of the move sequence, for every candidate move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never place a larger disk onto a peg that currently holds any smaller disk; first relocate those smaller disks elsewhere.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Immediately before moving a larger disk onto a peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 4 onto a peg that still has disk 1 on top, which is illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid moving small disks onto a peg that will later receive a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Do not place a small disk on a peg if a larger disk still needs to be moved onto that same peg later, as it will block the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When choosing a temporary destination for a small disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Putting disk 1 on a peg that later must receive disk 3, causing an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Move blocking smaller disks to any other peg before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk is not the topmost on its source peg, relocate the smaller disks above it to any other peg before moving the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever the desired larger disk is buried under smaller ones on its current peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 5 while disk 2 sits on top of it, resulting in an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Only preserve disks that are already in final position on the goal peg
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When scanning the goal peg, keep a disk only if all larger disks are already present below it on that peg; any disk that sits above a missing larger disk must be moved away before larger disks are placed.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the start of planning, after identifying the goal peg, check each disk on it for missing larger disks underneath.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Leaving disk 1 on the goal peg while larger disks 5 and 4 are still missing below it, which later blocks moving those larger disks.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model stops generation early or forgets to output the required list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always generate at least an empty list syntax "[]" and then fill it with moves before finishing.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of tokens or stops before finishing the full sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Plan the entire move sequence mentally, then output it in one block; avoid mid‑generation commentary that can cut off the list.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk based on goal position without checking the current stack order.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before adding a move, verify that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely moving a small disk onto the final target peg, causing later moves to be impossible
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model places a small disk on the goal peg before larger disks that need to go below it have been positioned.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Only place a small disk onto the final peg after all larger disks that belong below it are already there.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to place a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal move)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model forgets to clear smaller disks from the destination peg before moving a larger one.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always ensure the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
